Alaskan and subsistence fisherman here. Farmed salmon is extremely susceptible to parasites and disease. In the wild the infected fish are removed from the "harvest pool" and introduced into the natural cycle of life. In farms the parasites and diseases are permitted to be contained in the habitat of the healthy and thereby spread. Because of this, the "pool" of farmed fish has to be "pushed" by introducing higher density of fish and consequently higher food and waste.

Edit: also - there is also a high value to the efficiency of salmon spawning in a waterway. Oftentimes in the cases of sockeye and pinks the harvest has virtually no impact on future runs because of this. Chinook are the exception it seems.
